bullets.title: MU: Earnings Tonight with Street-High $1,625 PT; Buyside Expects $30+ Aug Q Guide
bullets.body: Micron reports FQ3 after the close with consensus EPS ~$20.83 on $35.85B revenue. UBS's Tim Arcuri carries a Street-high $1,625 PT with an EPS pathway to >$100; Jefferies models FQ4 guide ~$30 vs Street $24.3 with CY27 EPS ~$200 vs Street $122. ~75% of buyside surveyed expects MU above $1,000 post-print; key focus areas are Strategic Customer Agreements (60-70% DDR5 already locked long-term), ASP trajectory, and Aug Q guidance reset. Memory is described as the most consensus AI long in tech with elevated crowding and sell-the-news/leveraged-ETF risk flagged.

bullets.title: MU: Pre-Market +4.9%; Semi Selloff Tuesday Was Structural Not Fundamental
bullets.body: MU gained 4.9% in pre-market alongside SNDK +3.5%, CRDO +2.9%, MRVL +2.4%, ALAB +2.1%, and INTC +1.8%. Tuesday's SOX -7.87% (NDX 3rd largest daily pullback in a year) was attributed to Korean leveraged ETF flows (~$6B in MOC sales), quant/retail deleveraging, and HBM-to-DRAM rotation fears—not a change in AI narrative. SOX has moved ±5% on 8 of 16 June sessions but remains up ~5% for the month.

bullets.title: AMD: UBS Raises PT to $670; C2030 Server CPU Revenue Now $50B on Agentic AI
bullets.body: UBS raised AMD's PT to $670 (from $455) and ARM's to $470 (from $260), citing an architectural split where AMD captures outsized standalone agentic AI rack share (x86 advantage, core count) while ARM dominates latency-sensitive head nodes (~70% of ~20M unit TAM). AMD C2030E server CPU revenue raised to $50B from $41B; C27/C28 estimates lifted to $23B/$29B. UBS separately raises AMD C2030 server CPU to $50B and models ARM AGI CPU revenue at ~$14B with ~70% head-node share.

bullets.title: NVDA: China Black-Market Chip Prices Double; B300 Servers Hit ~$1M
bullets.body: Nvidia DGX B300 servers are trading at ~CNY7M (~$1M) on China's black market, roughly doubling since early 2026 due to US export crackdowns and robust demand from Chinese tech companies. Multiple sources (FT, StreetAccount, JPM, Jefferies) corroborate the surge. MS estimates NVDA CoWoS-L consumption could reach ~910k units in 2027 (+40% YoY) and its Vera CPU forecast at 5.75M units.

bullets.title: FOXA: UBS Buy; Soccer Drives Record $3.7B FY26 EBITDA; Trades <5x 2027/28E
bullets.body: UBS raises FOXA F4Q EBITDA estimate to $1.02B (vs consensus $975M) and full-year to a record $3.7B, incorporating ~$500M in World Cup ad revenue across F4Q/F1Q (up from $350M prior). Total company ad revenue seen +31% YoY in F4Q. Stock trades under 5x 2027/28 standalone EBITDA or 7.7x/6.6x pro forma with Roku. GS models F4Q EBITDA at $1.06B vs consensus $975M.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Joins DJIA June 29, Replacing VZ; Historical Avg -3% at T+5 Post-Inclusion
bullets.body: Alphabet officially replaces Verizon in the DJIA effective June 29. Jefferies notes historical DJIA additions average -3% at T+5 post-inclusion. GOOGL also lost two prominent AI researchers to rivals this week. JPM positions GOOGL alongside AMZN and SHOP as primary beneficiaries of agentic commerce, with AI-referred traffic growing 8-15x Y/Y and converting at 2x+ vs organic.

bullets.title: AMZN/SHOP/GOOGL: Agentic Commerce Driving 13x Order Growth; $12B Incremental AMZN Revenue
bullets.body: JPM frames GOOGL/AMZN/SHOP as the three-layer agentic commerce beneficiaries. AMZN's Rufus/Alexa for Shopping generated $12B incremental annualized revenue in 2025 (MAU +115% YoY); SHOP AI-referred shoppers convert 50% higher with 14% higher AOVs, orders growing 13x YoY. AI traffic <1% of e-commerce but growing 8-15x faster than industry and converts 42% better. ETSY agentic traffic grew 15x YoY in Q4.

bullets.title: CCL: 2Q Beat on Costs; FY26 Yield Guide Cut ~100bps on Middle East; June Bookings Recovering
bullets.body: CCL reported 2Q adj. EPS $0.41 vs guidance $0.34 and consensus $0.33; adj. EBITDA $1.582B vs guide $1.48B. FY26 net yield growth guidance cut to +1.75% c/c (from +2.75%) due to Middle East conflict impact on European sailings (43% of 3Q capacity). FY26 EPS held at $2.22. Management calls the May booking softness 'transitory' with June 'turning a corner.' JPM OW with $43 PT; Citi maintains Buy at $37; Hedgeye says CCL's issues are geographic/transitory with limited read-through to VIK/RCL.

bullets.title: TSM/Memory: Price Hikes Broadening; TSM +5-10% on 7nm and Below; DRAM Spot Rising
bullets.body: TSM is raising prices 5-10% on 7nm and below nodes as demand exceeds supply. MediaTek is raising chip prices 10-20% citing component shortages. DRAM spot prices rising (mainstream DDR4 +0.28%); 60-70% of DDR5 already locked in long-term supply contracts. Memory shortage only ~50% fulfilling customer demand; prices expected to rise through 2027. SK Hynix controls 57-61% of HBM market vs 21% for Micron.

bullets.title: SK Hynix $29.4B US ADR Filing (SKHY) Targets Nasdaq July 10
bullets.body: SK Hynix filed for a US ADR listing targeting $29.4B via 17.79M new shares at ~$145 each (10:1 ratio), beginning Nasdaq trading July 10. If priced at top end, would be the second-largest IPO after SpaceX. Proceeds fund Korean chip capacity, advanced packaging fab, and EUV scanners. Goldman Sachs is global coordinator; Citi, BofA, JPM are active bookrunners. Jefferies notes the listing could help SK Hynix narrow its valuation gap with Micron.

bullets.title: QCOM: Acquires Modular (AI-Native SW Stack); Investor Day Expectations Muted
bullets.body: Qualcomm entered a definitive agreement to acquire Modular Inc., an open AI-native software stack provider, for up to 19.2M QCOM shares via private placement, closing expected H2 2026. Separately, Citi survey shows 50% of buyside expects QCOM Investor Day to be a non-event, 25% expect 'sell the news.' UBS models QCOM data center narrative adding ~$20B to the existing model, targeting $65B revenue/$25 EPS in 5 years. QCOM also reportedly in talks to provide custom chip design to ByteDance via AlphaWave Semi technology.

bullets.title: META: Arena Prediction Market App; $299 Smart Glasses; No AI Safety Agreement
bullets.body: META is building Arena, an internal prediction market app (non-money initially, real money possible later), which sparked volatility in DKNG. META is also launching $299 smart glasses (Adventurer/Fury). Multiple sources note META is the only major US AI developer without a government AI safety review agreement and is facing Trump admin pressure. META/MSFT cited as leading a combined $850B data center lease boom.

bullets.title: PLTR: ZETA Partnership a 7-Year Foundry Deal; -1.8% Pre-Market
bullets.body: Citi reiterates Buy on ZETA (PT $26) after a 7-year partnership to rearchitect its Data Cloud on Palantir Foundry, targeting $100M+ ARR for Zeta and a live go-to-market by end of 3Q26. Cross-selling across PLTR's enterprise customer base and a path to 10x ROAS (vs current 6x) are the key catalysts. Separately, PLTR was down 1.8% in pre-market alongside NOW -1.4%, while semis broadly recovered.

bullets.title: CEG: WMT Nuclear Deal; Down 25% YTD on Hyperscaler BYOG Fears
bullets.body: Mizuho highlights Constellation Energy extending its nuclear partnership with Walmart, with capacity ramps beginning 2029-2030 in Illinois. CEG is down ~25% YTD on fears of stranded capacity from hyperscaler BYOG trends and utility competition from the NextEra/Dominion merger (which creates the largest regulated utility with 13 reactors). DOE committed $17.5B in low-cost loans for five nuclear projects but utilities remain unlikely to build new plants given 7-10 year payback timelines.

bullets.title: ORCL: Cuts 21,000 Employees (13% of Workforce) on AI Automation; NOW Price Hikes
bullets.body: Oracle is undergoing a major reduction in force of ~21,000 employees (13% of workforce) citing AI adoption and automation. Wolfe SaaS Daily separately notes ServiceNow is implementing price increases. IGV returned -15.7% YTD vs S&P 500 +10.1%; all-SaaS multiples down 2.22% WoW trading at 4.9x FY+2 EV/Sales.

bullets.title: STX/WDC: Klein Favors STX; HDD Sector Most Liked by Core Semi Investors
bullets.body: Mizuho's Klein is bullish long-term on STX and WDC, with STX preferred, citing HDD as one of the three most liked sub-sectors by core semi investors alongside Semi Cap Equipment and Analog. STX gained +1.8% and WDC +2.0% in pre-market trading. Klein prefers to wait for pullbacks before adding given 100%+ YTD semi rally and crowded positioning.

bullets.title: TSLA: JPM Projects $300B Robotaxi Revenue by 2035, $500B by 2040
bullets.body: JPM's tech digest frames TSLA's vision-only approach as deeply embedded with costly reversal risk. FSD v15 is ~5-6 months out. JPM projects TSLA robotaxi revenue at ~$300B by 2035 and ~$500B by 2040 with a 35M Cybercab fleet, positioning TSLA as a credible long-term autonomous mobility platform. UBER is cited as the key competitive read-through.

bullets.title: SNOW/PLTR/CRM: Data Infrastructure Favored Over Apps at Cannes '26
bullets.body: Citi's Cannes '26 midweek recap notes data infrastructure is viewed more positively than application software by customers; data modernization is the key AI adoption bottleneck. AI-native workflows and agents are seen disintermediating legacy seat-based models. SNOW, PLTR, and Databricks were among names most discussed at the conference; FROG ranked as a top-3 infrastructure software long per UBS investor feedback with PT raised to $92.

bullets.title: GOOGL/MSFT: JPM Derivatives Recommends Selling Puts as Tactical Buy on Pullback
bullets.body: JPM derivatives strategy recommends selling GOOGL and MSFT puts as target-buy positions, using the technical pullback to build exposure while monetizing rich implied volatility. They also recommend buying NDX>SPX or XLK>SPX outperformance calls for continued AI/tech leadership. US equity financing is at record non-year-end levels on strong leverage demand.

bullets.title: AMZN: Prime Day Sales -16% YoY; AWS CEO Bullish on AI ROI
bullets.body: Multiple sources flag AMZN Prime Day sales declining 16% year-over-year, a notable demand signal. Separately, AWS CEO stated 90% of CIOs are seeing materially positive ROI or a clear path to high ROI on AI investments vs. 0% a year ago, with AMZN AWS prioritizing high capex to maximize ROIC. Nokia expanded its AWS collaboration for autonomous networks (Level 4 autonomy) expected available later in 2026.
